name: Wikidata entity dumps directory (sizes)
what: Official Wikimedia listing of Wikidata entity dumps. Latest dated directory shown is 20261012.
why_it_matters: Sets disk and download budget for a humans+orgs T0 extract from the full dump instead of the live API.
numbers: latest-all.json.bz2 = 103,409,622,204 bytes (~103 GB); latest-truthy.nt.bz2 = 43,534,958,911 bytes (~43.5 GB); latest-all.nt.bz2 = 196,233,094,777 bytes (~196 GB); latest-all.ttl.bz2 = 125,778,820,821 bytes (~126 GB). Source: directory listing fetched 2026-10-14. Meta dump page says Jan 2026 uncompressed size 1.6 TB (https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Data_dumps/Dumps_sizes_and_growth).
ui_notes: Pick latest-truthy.nt.bz2 for a smaller first pass (best-rank direct values only, no qualifiers); pick latest-all.json.bz2 when qualifiers or sitelinks are needed.
note: Sizes are compressed bytes from the directory listing; uncompressed is roughly 1.6 TB per Meta.

name: Wikidata:Database download (formats, tools, incremental)
what: Official page listing Wikidata dump formats, licence and third-party readers.
why_it_matters: Canonical source for CC0 licence of structured data and for the incremental-dump location.
numbers: JSON dumps are weekly; incremental dumps cover about one day each at https://dumps.wikimedia.org/other/incr/wikidatawiki/. Tools named on page: wdumper, qwikidata (Python), JsonDumpReader (PHP), gitlab.com/tozd/go/mediawiki (Go), WDSub (Scala), simple-wikidata-db (Python), wd2sql (Rust, JSON dump to SQLite). Page gives an academictorrents example of 130.53 GiB for wikidata-20240101-all.json.gz (fetched 2026-10-14).
note: wikidata-filter, KGTK and QLever are NOT mentioned on this page; do not cite it for them.

name: Wikimedia EventStreams recentchange (incremental feed)
what: Server-sent-events stream of recent changes across Wikimedia wikis, including wikidatawiki; backed by Kafka; resumable from stream position.
why_it_matters: Lets the people+orgs graph keep T0 current between weekly dumps by replaying edits for Q5 and org-class items.
numbers: Endpoint stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange (per search result, not fetched). Pywikibot EventStreams example filters type=edit, wiki=wikidatawiki.
note: Endpoint string came from a search snippet; check on wikitech before relying on it. The stream carries edits, not full entity JSON.

name: QLever SPARQL endpoint for Wikidata
what: Public QLever SPARQL service over Wikidata, faster than WDQS for counting and large scans; needs explicit PREFIX declarations.
why_it_matters: Counts can be taken without a dump; good for sanity-checking T0 totals and for pulling subsets in pages.
numbers: Measured 2026-10-14: COUNT of ?x wdt:P31 wd:Q5 = 13,738,078 humans. COUNT DISTINCT of ?x wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q43229 = 4,986,530 organisation-class items. Same query on query.wikidata.org (WDQS) returned 4,986,579 for the org count; WDQS timed out on the human count.
note: Counts differ by about 50 between QLever and WDQS, consistent with a different snapshot time. Full-text index claim was NOT verified.

name: DBpedia ontology and live SPARQL endpoint
what: DBpedia ontology page with class-instance counts, plus the live endpoint at dbpedia.org/sparql.
why_it_matters: DBpedia is a free, linkable person and organisation source with multilingual labels; useful as a cross-reference and label source.
numbers: Ontology page (undated, fetched 2026-10-14): Person 1,592,912; Organisation 317,867. Live endpoint measured 2026-10-14: COUNT DISTINCT ?x a dbo:Person with an English rdfs:label = 1,277,612 (a plain COUNT without the label filter returned 5,056,927, which likely mixes graphs; do not use it).
note: The ontology page does not name a release number. Latest release (2025-06 announced) figures did not render; use live endpoint counts for now.

name: DBpedia licence statement
what: Official DBpedia about page licence statement.
why_it_matters: Share-alike obligations apply if DBpedia-derived rows are published.
numbers: States data is under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 and GNU Free Documentation License (fetched 2026-10-14).
note: Ontology page did not state a licence; the about page is the authority found here.

name: Pantheon data downloads (2.0 person files and 1.0 legacy)
what: Pantheon download page: Person Dataset CSVs for 2019, 2020, 2025 (Pantheon 2.0) plus 1.0 legacy TSVs.
why_it_matters: Only public, ready-made person table with an occupation, HPI-style score, birth/death places and a Wikidata id (wd_id), which can join straight to Wikidata Q5.
numbers: person_2025_update.csv.bz2: 126,582 person rows (126,583 lines incl. header), 12,354,476 bytes compressed, 38,931,553 bytes uncompressed (counted 2026-10-14 by streaming download). person_2020_update: 7,928,528 bytes compressed (rows not counted). legacy_pantheon.tsv.bz2: 643,495 bytes. Site text says it has data on more than 85,000 biographies, which conflicts with 126k rows.
ui_notes: Columns include id, wd_id, wp_id, slug, name, occupation, prob_ratio, gender, twitter, alive, l, hpi_raw, birthplace/deathplace with lat/lon and geonameid, birthyear, deathyear. Use wd_id as the join key to Wikidata.
note: Licence for the 2.0 files is NOT stated on the dataset page; the footer shows CC BY-SA 4.0 but does not tie it to the files. Ask or check /en/data/permissions before redistributing.

name: Pantheon 1.0: a manually verified dataset of globally famous biographies (Yu et al., 2016)
what: Paper describing the Pantheon 1.0 dataset and the Historical Popularity Index (HPI). Published in Scientific Data 2:150075, doi 10.1038/sdata.2015.75.
why_it_matters: Defines how HPI is built (languages, pageviews, age); needed to explain any popularity score in the graph.
numbers: 11,341 biographies with more than 25 Wikipedia language editions; pageviews 2008-2013 (Yu et al., per search snippets, 2016). Paper licence CC BY 4.0 (arXiv PDF text, fetched by search 2026-10-14).
note: The exact HPI Equation 4 with weights was NOT retrieved (PDF fetch exceeded size limit; Nature page redirected to login). Approximation in the 2025 GDP paper (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.09399): log10(V) + ln(L) + log4(A), minus (70-A)/7 when A<70; R^2=0.76 against Pantheon HPI. Treat as approximation only.

name: Research Organization Registry (ROR)
what: Open registry of research organisation IDs with names, types, relationships and external IDs; API and data dumps; updated at least monthly.
why_it_matters: Clean, CC0 org-ID backbone for the academic and research-institution slice of the org graph.
numbers: API api.ror.org/v2/organizations reports number_of_results = 141,387 (measured 2026-10-14). Zenodo v2.5 dump record (31 Mar 2026) lists 124,882 research organisations (https://zenodo.org/records/19356124, from search snippet). The gap between the two is unexplained; check which one the dump counts.
note: Licence CC0 1.0 stated on ror.org. Count discrepancy between the API and the Zenodo record should be resolved before quoting either.

name: GLEIF LEI records and Golden Copy
what: Legal-entity identifier database with Level 1 (who is who), Level 2 (parent relationships) and reporting exceptions, published as Golden Copy files.
why_it_matters: Authoritative legal-entity list for companies and funds worldwide; the best free org-entity spine with parent links.
numbers: GLEIF LEI API api.gleif.org/api/v1/lei-records total = 3,460,635 (measured 2026-10-14). Golden Copy issued three sets of files daily (GLEIF download page). Q2 2026 business report: 87.9% of the LEI population fully corroborated Level 1 data (https://www.gleif.org/lei-data/global-lei-index/download-global-lei-system-business-reports/download-global-lei-system-business-report-q2-2026/q2-2026-quarterly_business_report.pdf).
note: CC0 licence for GLEIF data was only seen in a third-party API doc; NOT confirmed on a GLEIF page. Verify before stating it.

name: OpenCorporates terms of use (licence for bulk and API)
what: OpenCorporates licence: database under ODbL; site content under CC BY-SA; free use limited to Permitted Users; bulk by contact.
why_it_matters: Shows that bulk company data is share-alike and commercially restricted; a graph that ingests it inherits ODbL share-alike.
numbers: No company count on the page. Free access: journalists, NGOs and academics doing public-benefit research and the public for personal use. Corporations, financial institutions, government bodies are not Permitted Users. Attribution must be a hyperlink reading from OpenCorporates. Automated scraping prohibited except search indexation (fetched 2026-10-14).
note: Bulk terms are 'contact us'; the bulk page says a free global file is possible if results are shared under the open licence (per search snippet).

name: Harmonic.ai (company and people database, API)
what: Commercial startup and people database with API, MCP server and bulk import to a warehouse.
why_it_matters: Largest commercial startup-company dataset in this list; benchmark for how much org+people coverage a paid feed gives.
numbers: Vendor pricing page: 20M+ companies and 150M+ people from legal filings and public sources. Newer vendor comparison: 35M+ companies and 195M+ profiles (https://harmonic.ai/blog/top-crunchbase-competitors-and-alternatives-in-2026). Dealroom listing: 20M+ companies, 160M individuals. Vendor-stated; no audit found.
note: Refresh claims conflict (daily for priority companies vs every 3-4 months per a review). Commercial licence; no bulk redistribution.

name: Dealroom.co (tech companies and investors)
what: Commercial dataset of technology companies and investors with export credits and an API on the Enterprise tier.
why_it_matters: Europe-strong tech company and investor coverage; a paid cross-check for startup org rows.
numbers: Current pricing page: Premium EUR 12,500/yr (10,000 export credits per user); Premium Plus EUR 17,000/yr (Zapier or API); Enterprise custom with full API and MCP server. Older 2024 page showed Starter EUR 12,000. Profile count of 4M+ is a third-party claim, not verified (fetched via search 2026-10-14).
note: Prices are as shown on the cited pages; API price not published.

name: Muck Rack (journalist and media database)
what: PR and media database of journalists and outlets, sold with custom quotes.
why_it_matters: Only journalist-centric people database in this gap list; relevant to the people side for media figures.
numbers: No journalist count found. Pricing is quote-only; third-party estimates: Rephonic (Dec 2025) basic annual plan about USD 258/mo, Pro annual about USD 416/mo; SpendHound (160 customers) average SMB USD 12,874/yr and enterprise USD 78,996/yr.
note: No primary Muck Rack page was fetched; all numbers are third-party. API licence not found.

name: Clay (GTM data waterfall)
what: Workflow layer that queries many external data providers in sequence (a waterfall); not a proprietary person or org database.
why_it_matters: Clarifies that a '100M+ contacts' Clay claim is not a database to ingest; provider waterfall is an enrichment pattern, not a source of truth.
numbers: Clay marketplace says 200+ providers in one waterfall (vendor page, fetched via search 2026-10-14). Reviews cite 150+ providers. Reported find-rate test: 40% to 78% email find rate (third-party review). No primary count of Clay's own records found.
note: The 100M+ contacts figure could not be verified and should not be used.

name: LinkedIn Economic Graph (Data for Impact and research program)
what: Public face of LinkedIn Economic Graph: anonymised aggregate indicators shared with partners; academic access is aggregate-only in a secure sandbox.
why_it_matters: Confirms there is no public person-level or company-level LinkedIn dump; any LinkedIn-derived graph would have to use the public web or licensed partners.
numbers: Indicators are anonymised and aggregated; partners include World Bank, IDB, IMF, OECD, Destatis, UNDP. Research program: aggregate, anonymised data only, no downloads (search snippets; program coverage mostly 2018-era).
note: Indicator list not fetched; the current menu needs a live check.

name: Golden.com (business intelligence and people or company profiles)
what: Business-intelligence platform that builds company and executive profiles, with API access described by a directory listing.
why_it_matters: Possible enrichment source for org and exec rows; alive status is only weakly evidenced.
numbers: Directory says millions of companies; API exists; pricing on request. No counts from Golden itself. Fetched via search 2026-10-14.
note: Still-alive status NOT confirmed by a Golden page. Only directory listings were found.
